idea: You can do anything, but not everything: pour your effort into one thing and it fills up; spread it across everything and nothing fills. For students abroad juggling study, part-time work and settling in, pick what matters most this term.

title: You can do anything, but not everything
Nobody hands you a report card after university
idea:
At university someone grades you every semester.

Picture a vintage report card headed Semester 1 2 3 4, graded for the first semester: Academic Writing A, Professional Communication A, Statistics 101 C, Research Methods B, Microeconomics B, Design Thinking A, Business Ethics A, Data Analysis C. Its key reads A = Excellent, B = Good, C = Satisfactory, N = Needs Improvement.

Now picture the same report card for life after university, headed Role, with the same eight rows and the same key: Husband, Son, Dog parent, Product Manager and Citizen, then three empty rows, and no grades at all.

After university the roles multiply and nobody hands you a report card. You have to decide for yourself what doing well means in each one.

text.heading: Semester 1 report card

text.heading: Life report card
text.body: Husband, Son, Dog parent, Product Manager, Citizen, then three empty rows. The same key, and no grades at all.

title: Balance is a process. Not a destination.
idea: For students abroad, study, part-time work and life never split the same way two weeks running. Some weeks are all study, some are mostly life. Balance is something you keep adjusting, not a place you arrive.
